title: Chair's Statement of the United States G20 Presidency
summary: G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors met on April 16, 2026 in Washington, D.C., to discuss economic impacts of the Middle East conflict on agriculture, value chains, and fertilizer markets. Members emphasized the importance of keeping food and fertilizer supply chains open for vulnerable countries and discussed the potential for coordinated macroeconomic policy responses to promote food security and market stability.
key_points: G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors met in Washington, D.C. on April 16, 2026 to discuss economic impacts of Middle East conflict
Members raised concerns about disruptions to agriculture markets, value chains, and fertilizer supply
Members emphasized avoiding export prohibitions or restrictions on fertilizers to protect low-income countries
IMF and World Bank Group committed to coordinating responses to economic impacts
Members discussed diversified fertilizer production to buffer poorest nations from food trade disruptions
US G20 Presidency committed to hosting further discussions on food and fertilizer in coming weeks
why_it_matters: This statement signals G20 attention to potential food security risks from Middle East conflict disruptions, but contains no concrete policy commitments or specific action items. It reflects diplomatic discussions rather than market-moving announcements.
macro_context: The G20 communiqué highlights concerns about fertilizer and food supply chain disruptions stemming from Middle East tensions. While members expressed willingness to coordinate macroeconomic policy responses, no specific fiscal or monetary measures were announced. The discussion of diversified fertilizer production and open supply chains could be relevant for agricultural commodity markets if disruptions materialize.
